source.title: Your AI, On a Dial: Controlling Investment Bias in LLMs with a Single Neuron
source.authors: Sahong Park; Suhwan Park; Hoyoung Lee; Gakyung Kwon; Wonbin Ahn; Jaewon Choi; Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Yoon Kim; Chanyeol Choi; Hyeongwoo Kong; Yongjae Lee

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a single MLP coordinate as an inference-time control for investment stance and reports how its dial performs. It does not test whether neurons have one interpretable job, audit neuron poles, evaluate explanation fidelity on held-out activations, or build attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports single-coordinate investment-bias steering, but its results do not measure the neuron interpretability, pole-level job counts, or explanation quality named by V1–V7. The dial's investment-control results are related to neuron-level control but do not test any listed version. Reported benchmark preservation, prompt comparisons, retrieval effects, long-context behavior, and portfolio outcomes concern the paper's own method and are not rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study selects one MLP coordinate per model by gradient sensitivity and calibration error and uses it as an additive steering dial for investment stance. It reports the dial's steering range, calibration, benchmark preservation and downstream effects. It never asks what the neuron's main job is, audits neuron poles, scores explanations on held-out activations, or builds neuron attribution graphs. Steering by a selected coordinate is not a test of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a single activation coordinate gives monotonic, model-specific, calibratable control of aggregate investment stance in five models, with no systematic benchmark degradation. They also report effects on information seeking, long-context stability and portfolio outcomes, with the backtest exploratory and not establishing alpha.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a fixed offset to one MLP coordinate at inference time to steer investment decisions; it does not use neuron-pole explanation, held-out explanation testing, or attribution-graph reconstruction methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected coordinate and response direction vary by model; reachable range is narrower for DeepSeek-R1-14B. The paper also reports that long-context prompt steering attenuates while dial steering remains stable in its tested setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In five open-weight LLMs, an additive shift to one MLP coordinate (chosen by gradient sensitivity and held-out calibration RMSE) moves aggregate buy–sell bias monotonically. Reachable ranges are model-dependent, and no benchmark decline survives BH correction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single selected MLP coordinate can serve as a monotonic, calibratable steering dial for an aggregate decision prior in LLMs.

record.problems: The study does not assess neuron interpretability or explanation fidelity. Its findings are specific to the tested models, investment tasks, activation coordinates, prompts, and intervention ranges; the authors also describe the portfolio backtest as exploratory.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted for the paper's benchmark-preservation, retrieval-agent, long-context, prompt-baseline, or portfolio results because they measure performance of the study's investment-control method, not any listed claim version about neuron interpretability or explanation.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or shares of main-job, two-job or unexplained neurons.
Five models are used, including the MoE model Llama-4-Scout, but no interpretable-neuron shares are measured in any of them.
No vision models, no InceptionV1 cat/car analysis, and no superposition analysis.
No comparison of interpretability across architectures or tools, and no vision estimates.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No explanations of the selected neurons are given or tested against held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: The title says 'single neuron', but the neuron is chosen for steerability, not for interpretability, and the paper offers no account of what it represents. The authors also note that the one-coordinate edit induces a dense residual-stream update (Table 7 note). Nothing here bears on whether neurons are monosemantic or explainable. All rows are method-performance values and should stay unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles, main-job shares, or unexplained poles.
No cross-model or scale assessment of neuron interpretability shares, including dense or mixture-of-experts models up to trillions of parameters.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No test of architecture, regularization, or tools as causes of neuron interpretability, and no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether neuron-based graphs explain behavior without a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict activation on new examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
